points.description: States abstraction as a main advantage of object-oriented programming (the student names abstraction, or clearly describes it as hiding complex detail and exposing only what is needed).
points.partial_credit: half marks for a vague or related idea, such as hiding details or simplifying code, without naming abstraction

points.description: States reusability as a main advantage of object-oriented programming (the student names reusability, or clearly describes reusing existing classes or code).
points.partial_credit: half marks for a vague mention, such as code can be used again, without linking it to classes or objects

rubric.notes: Full marks need both abstraction and reusability named as advantages of object-oriented programming. Abstraction carries 3 marks and reusability 2 marks, and each is judged separately, so a wrong or missing point does not reduce the other. Extra correct advantages such as encapsulation or inheritance are fine but do not replace either required point; a wrong advantage stated alongside them does not cancel a correct point.
